---
title: Handle files
description: Upload a file's bytes, make the item that names them, download them, hand out a link that expires, and replace them.
---

A file comes in two parts: a blob, which is the bytes, and a file item that names the blob by its hash and carries the title and everything else. Upload the bytes first, then create the item. From then on, anyone who can read the item can read the bytes. [Files](/build/files) explains why the two are apart.

To upload, your key needs write on at least one type outside `system.*`, or the `blobs.manage` permission; with neither, Marfa answers `403 type_not_permitted`. To create the file item, it needs write on the item's type, such as `core.file`. In the TypeScript examples, `marfa` is a client made as [the TypeScript SDK](/typescript-sdk#create-a-client) shows. In the Swift examples, `copy` is an [open working copy](/swift-sdk/working-copy#open-a-copy).

## Upload the bytes

[Upload a blob](/api-reference/blobs/uploadBlob) takes the bytes as the request body, **as they are rather than as a form**, with their media type as the `Content-Type`:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa blobs upload reading-list.txt
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /blobs
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: text/plain

<the bytes of reading-list.txt>
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
import { readFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const { data: blob, error } = await marfa.POST("/blobs", {
  body: await readFile("reading-list.txt"),
  headers: { "Content-Type": "text/plain" },
});
if (error) throw new Error(error.error.message);
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let upload = try await copy.blobs.put(file: fileURL, mimeType: "text/plain")
guard let hash = upload.blob else { return }
```

Marfa answers with the blob's `hash`, the media type it will serve the bytes under, and their size:

```json title="Response" status="201"
{
  "hash": "sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0",
  "mime_type": "text/plain",
  "size_bytes": 34
}
```

The same bytes always give the same hash, so uploading them again **stores nothing new**. An upload adds no [event](/build/events): the item you create next does.

An upload has **no size cap and no total time limit**. Marfa ends one with `408 request_timeout` only when no bytes arrive for 60 seconds. While a store is still writing or deleting the same bytes, an upload answers `503 blob_store_unavailable`: try again shortly.

## Point an item at the bytes

Create a file item whose **`blob_ref`** is the hash. `core.file` takes any file. Use `core.file.image`, `core.file.audio`, `core.file.video` or `core.file.webpage` (an HTML page held as a file) where they fit, or a type of your own beneath `core.file`.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa items create --type core.file --prop title=reading-list.txt \
  --prop blob_ref=sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0 \
  --prop mime_type=text/plain
```

```http tab="HTTP"
POST /items
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "type": "core.file",
  "properties": {
    "title": "reading-list.txt",
    "blob_ref": "sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0",
    "mime_type": "text/plain"
  }
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data: created } = await marfa.POST("/items", {
  body: {
    type: "core.file",
    properties: { title: "reading-list.txt", blob_ref: blob.hash, mime_type: blob.mime_type },
  },
});
```

```swift tab="Swift"
_ = try await copy.items.create(Draft(
    type: "core.file",
    properties: ["title": "reading-list.txt", "blob_ref": .string(hash), "mime_type": "text/plain"]))
```

Marfa sets the item's `size_bytes` from the stored bytes. Soon after, a housekeeping job reads the bytes and adds what it finds that the item lacks, such as `extracted_text` or an image's `width` and `height`, which moves the item to its next version.

`marfa items add reading-list.txt` uploads the bytes and creates the item in one command, and chooses the subtype from the media type unless you name one.

**Until an item names the hash, the bytes can't be read**, even with the key that uploaded them; only the owner and a key with `blobs.manage` can. A file item may name only bytes its writer uploaded or can already read. Any other hash in `blob_ref` is refused `404 blob_not_found`, the same answer as a hash nothing holds, so the refusal never tells you whether the instance has the bytes. Upload with **the same key** that writes the item. A hash in any other property, such as an image link in a note's body, is taken as text. It lets readers of the item read the blob only if the writer uploaded the bytes or could already read them, as [Files](/build/files#who-may-read-a-blob) explains.

## Attach a file to an item

To attach a file to a note or any other item, link them with an `attached-to` edge from the file item, as `marfa items attach <id> photo.jpg` does in one command. The file is then an **attachment**: it goes to the bin with the last item it's attached to, and comes back with any of them. [Edges](/build/edges) says how that works.

On a device, a working copy also links a body that shows the file, with `![](path)` or `![[file]]`, to it with a `references` edge. That edge **embeds** the file and attaches nothing.

## Find a file by its text

Once the housekeeping job has written a file item's `extracted_text`, [search](/build/list-filter-search#search) finds the file by any word in it:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa search quokka --type core.file
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /search?q=quokka&type=core.file
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

The job runs every 30 seconds, so a new file is found by its `title`, `description` and tags first, and by its text a little later. It reads plain text and Markdown, web pages, PDFs, Word, Excel and PowerPoint files and their OpenDocument equivalents, and images while OCR is on. The instance's [configuration](/run/settings#change-settings-while-it-runs) turns it off (`enrichment_enabled`), turns OCR off (`enrichment_ocr_enabled`) and limits the text it keeps (`enrichment_max_text_chars`).

## Download the bytes

[Download a blob](/api-reference/blobs/downloadBlob) answers the bytes as they were uploaded:

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa blobs download sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0 --output reading-list.txt
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /blobs/sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
import { writeFile } from "node:fs/promises";

const { data: bytes } = await marfa.GET("/blobs/{hash}", {
  params: { path: { hash: blob.hash } },
  parseAs: "arrayBuffer",
});
await writeFile("reading-list.txt", Buffer.from(bytes!));
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let bytes = try await copy.blobs.withFile(hash) { url in try Data(contentsOf: url) }
```

Marfa sends the bytes as an attachment named after the hash, never as a page a browser would show, so take the file's name from the item's **`title`**. A `Range` header such as `bytes=0-1023` gets part of a blob, with `206`.

A blob you may not read answers `404 blob_not_found`, as a hash that doesn't exist does. `503 blob_store_unavailable` means no store could answer, so Marfa can't tell whether the bytes are gone: try again later.

A working copy fetches the bytes for you and keeps them, as [Keep files on a device](/build/keep-files-on-a-device) shows. In the Swift SDK, read the file inside the `withFile` closure: the copy can remove it afterward.

## Hand out a time-limited link

An image element in a web page can't send your key. [Get a blob URL](/api-reference/blobs/getBlobUrl) answers a link that serves the bytes to anyone who has it, until it expires. `ttl_seconds` is its lifetime: **an hour by default, and at most seven days**. Marfa shortens a longer one to seven days, and the answer says what you got.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa blobs url sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0 --ttl-seconds 900
```

```http tab="HTTP"
GET /blobs/sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0/url?ttl_seconds=900
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data: link } = await marfa.GET("/blobs/{hash}/url", {
  params: { path: { hash: blob.hash }, query: { ttl_seconds: 900 } },
});
```

```json title="Response" status="200"
{
  "url": "http://localhost:8600/blobs/sha256:4b140644d197859760a999df9121a6a840edd1dadc6142a413f6dcd108c898a0/fetch?expires=1795048602794&signature=ea09307e75f2e6a367dfb3662577f47381d47c226e288ec89137113e984ad12a",
  "ttl_seconds": 900
}
```

Marfa checks your read **when it makes the link**, not when someone fetches it. Revoking your key, or deleting every item that names the blob, doesn't end a link early. So ask for a link when you need one, with the shortest lifetime that serves, and **don't store it**.

## Replace a file's bytes

Upload the new bytes, then update the file item's `blob_ref` to the new hash, **naming the version you read**, as [Write safely](/build/write-safely) shows. **Clear what housekeeping read from the old bytes** in the same write, here `extracted_text`, and for an image `width` and `height` too: housekeeping only fills a field the item lacks, so a value from the old bytes would stay.

```bash tab="CLI" tab-group="client"
marfa blobs upload reading-list.txt
marfa items update <id> --version 2 \
  --prop blob_ref=sha256:7623dfe0bbb9b127e9d68350ac7d9168fecfb3ac404778057b116315d3205780 \
  --clear-property extracted_text
```

```http tab="HTTP"
PATCH /items/<id>
Authorization: Bearer $MARFA_API_KEY
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "version": 2,
  "properties": {
    "blob_ref": "sha256:7623dfe0bbb9b127e9d68350ac7d9168fecfb3ac404778057b116315d3205780"
  },
  "clear_properties": ["extracted_text"]
}
```

```ts tab="TypeScript"
const { data: newBlob } = await marfa.POST("/blobs", {
  body: await readFile("reading-list.txt"),
  headers: { "Content-Type": "text/plain" },
});
await marfa.PATCH("/items/{id}", {
  params: { path: { id } },
  body: {
    version: 2,
    properties: { blob_ref: newBlob!.hash },
    clear_properties: ["extracted_text"],
  },
});
```

```swift tab="Swift"
let replacement = try await copy.blobs.put(file: newFileURL, mimeType: "text/plain")
guard let newHash = replacement.blob, let item = try await copy.items.get(id) else { return }
_ = try await copy.items.update(id, Edit(
    properties: ["blob_ref": .string(newHash)], clearProperties: ["extracted_text"],
    baseVersion: item.version))
```

Marfa sets the new `size_bytes`, and the housekeeping job then reads the new bytes into `extracted_text`. The old blob stays **as long as an earlier version** of the item names it. Once nothing names it, a later housekeeping run purges it, at least `blob_cleanup_grace_seconds` after it was found unnamed, a day by default, and never while a backup still names it.

The rules behind this guide are in the [blobs](https://github.com/withmarfa/marfa/blob/main/conformance/spec/blobs.md) chapter of the contract.
